formation.title: The Crown of Two Realms
formation.text:
From the rough cliffs of Northumbria to the sun-warmed vineyards of the Garonne, the lions of the Plantagenets now reign over a single house of dominions. Henry's bequest, gathered by inheritance, marriage and conquest, defies every map of Christendom: an empire that knows no language and answers to no peer.

Yet the Angevin Empire is no kingdom in any received sense. London speaks the rough English of the Saxon shires; Rouen and Caen speak the langue d'oil of the Norman barons; Poitiers and Bordeaux sing in the Occitan of the troubadours; Angers obeys an angevin steward; Dublin and Wexford answer a Norman lord through Welsh marcher captains. To rule them all the King must choose how he shall rule.

Some at court urge a kingdom of one law: the royal writ, the King's Bench, the Exchequer of Westminster reaching across the Channel, a crown that flattens custom into a single common right. Others, marshalled by the great barons of Normandy, Aquitaine and the Marches, urge a federation of fiefs: the King as the supreme suzerain among peers, his realm a tapestry of feudal courts, tournaments and homage given freely.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: One king, one law, one writ across the Channel

modifiers.name: Common Law of the Crown
modifiers.text: Royal writs, justices in eyre and the Exchequer of Westminster bind the duchies into a single jurisdiction. Customs bow to the King's law.

options.text: A confederacy of barons under a chivalric crown

modifiers.name: Chivalric Confederation
modifiers.text: The King reigns as suzerain among magnates. Tournaments, oaths of homage and feudal hosts make the realm formidable in arms even as it remains a patchwork of custom.

advances.name: Exchequer of Westminster
advances.text: The pipe rolls and the chequered cloth: Roger of Salisbury's exchequer turns royal accounts into the most sophisticated fiscal instrument in twelfth-century Europe.

advances.name: Assize Courts and Royal Justices
advances.text: Henry II's reforms send royal justices riding the realm. Disputes over land, homicide and theft now flow up to the crown rather than dissipating in seignorial halls.

event.title: The Assize of Clarendon
event.text:
At the council of Clarendon Henry has summoned bishops, barons and royal justices to a hunting lodge in Wiltshire. The chequered cloth of the Exchequer is unrolled. Justices in eyre are commissioned to ride the realm: to inquire by sworn juries of presentment into hidden murders, robberies and the receivers of malefactors. From this hour forward, the law of the King flows where the King's writ runs.

For a generation no royal court has reached so deep into the shires; for a century no royal justice has bound the duchies of the continent into a single jurisprudence. The judges depart for their circuits before the candles burn out.

options.text: Let the King's law ride into every shire

modifiers.name: Assize of Clarendon
modifiers.text: The royal courts circulate through the realm; juries of presentment reveal hidden malefactors. Order travels with the King's justices.

advances.name: Marcher Castles
advances.text: The chains of stone keeps along the Welsh marches and the Norman frontier. Concentric fortification carried from the East by the Plantagenets and their Norman engineers.

advances.name: Welsh Archers in Royal Service
advances.text: The longbowmen of Gwent and Powys, kept on royal contract since the Welsh campaigns. The black-fletched arrows that pierced French mail at every Plantagenet field.

advances.name: Norman Chivalry
advances.text: Mounted men-at-arms in long mail hauberks, scions of the conquering Norman aristocracy. The shock arm of the Plantagenet host.

advances.name: Forest Law
advances.text: The royal forests, vast preserves under direct crown jurisdiction. Verderers, regarders and the harsh forest courts produce hated revenue and an unparalleled royal demesne.

advances.name: Brabançons and Routiers
advances.text: The Flemish and Lowland mercenary companies that fought for the highest Angevin bidder. Disciplined, professional, and feared, the standing edge of the Plantagenet army.

advances.name: Gascon Crossbowmen
advances.text: The crossbow militias of Bordeaux, Bayonne and the Gascon ports. Foot crossbowmen who shielded the wine fleets and held the southern marches.

advances.name: Courtly Love and the Troubadours
advances.text: Eleanor of Aquitaine's court at Poitiers: Marie de France, Bernart de Ventadorn, Chrétien de Troyes. The chivalric romance refined and exported across Christendom.

event.title: The Court at Poitiers
event.text:
Eleanor (Queen of England, Duchess of Aquitaine, Countess of Poitou) has taken her household to her own city of Poitiers. About her gather the troubadours of the south: Bernart de Ventadorn, the polished Marie de France, the young Chrétien de Troyes. They sing of fin amor: of an exalted, almost ritual love between knight and lady that subordinates feudal violence to courtly grace.

The knightly culture of Poitiers will travel back across the Channel with the Queen's chamberlains and minstrels. From this court will come the cycle of Arthur and the Holy Grail, the rules of the tournament, the very vocabulary of romance. The world of feudal Christendom is being courteously remade.

options.text: Refine our chivalry: knighthood as the Queen would have it

modifiers.name: Courts of Love
modifiers.text: Eleanor's court at Poitiers reshapes the manners of Christendom. Troubadours, romance and courtly love transform the chivalric ideal.

advances.name: Assize of Arms
advances.text: The Assize of Arms of 1181: every freeman to be equipped according to his estate. The basis of a national militia three centuries before any peer.

advances.name: Bordeaux Wine Trade
advances.text: The fleets that carry Gascon claret from Bordeaux to London, a Channel-spanning trade that binds Aquitaine to the English crown by silver as much as by oath.

advances.name: Cinque Ports Confederation
advances.text: Hastings, Sandwich, Dover, Romney, Hythe: the towns sworn to provide ships for the King in exchange for charters of self-government. The Channel fleet by feudal contract.

advances.name: Charter Towns and Burgesses
advances.text: Henry II and his sons grant borough charters across the realm. Self-governing communes of merchants under royal protection, the seedbed of urban liberty.

advances.name: Massed Longbow Tactics
advances.text: The doctrine of arrow storms over advancing cavalry, practised at Falkirk, perfected at Crécy. The disciplined longbow archer in deep ranks.

advances.name: Estates of Aquitaine
advances.text: Customary parlements of Bordeaux, Poitiers and Saintes, where Gascon nobles, prelates and townsmen consented to ducal taxation. A constitutional precedent.

advances.name: The Chancellor's Writ
advances.text: The standardised royal writ runs throughout England and the duchies. The bureaucracy of the King's Chancery becomes the spine of trans-Channel governance.

event.title: The Constitutions of Clarendon
event.text:
Henry has summoned his bishops to set in writing the customs of his grandfather's reign. The Constitutions return to crown the trial of clerks who commit felony, the appeal of bishops to Rome only by royal leave, the King's voice in the election of prelates. Thomas Becket has affixed his seal, and then taken it back.

The quarrel between altar and throne is an old one in Latin Christendom, but no king before Henry has dared to codify the privileges of the crown so plainly against the immunities of the Church. Where now lies the King's edge?

options.text: Press the crown's writ: the King makes prelates as he makes earls

modifiers.name: Erastian Crown
modifiers.text: The crown asserts itself over the prelacy. Bishops are royal officers in mitre.

options.text: Strike a concordat: the King who wins the Church wins all

modifiers.name: Concordat of Clarendon
modifiers.text: King and Church speak with one voice. The clergy preach for the crown.

advances.name: Cogs of the Angevin Channel
advances.text: The clinker-built Channel cogs of Sandwich and Rouen, the workhorses of a thalassocratic merchant marine, carrying English wool, Gascon wine and Norman herring.

event.title: The Battle of the Channel
event.text:
Off the cliffs of the South Foreland, the Angevin fleet of the Cinque Ports has met the foe in the narrow sea. Cogs of Sandwich and Hythe, sails black against the autumn sky, drive the longships of the enemy into the white surf of the chalk. The Channel henceforth belongs to the Angevin admiral.

No king of the West has held both shores of the narrow sea since the Romans. Now the salt water that once divided the Plantagenet realm becomes its inland highway.

options.text: Master the Channel: let the wool fleets sail unmolested

advances.name: Writ of Summons
advances.text: Magnates summoned by name to attend the King's council. The seed of a parliamentary tradition that would outlive the Angevin polity itself.

event.title: Runnymede
event.text:
On the meadow at Runnymede, between Windsor and Staines, the King has met the assembled barons of the realm in arms. After Bouvines and the loss of Normandy the magnates will be forced no longer; they have drawn up a charter of liberties: sixty-three clauses guaranteeing baronial counsel, the privileges of the Church, the customs of London, the freedom of merchants and the lawful judgment of peers.

Will the crown grant the charter, accept the limits of its prerogative and bind the magnates to faith? Or will it stake everything on royal arms, stand against the demand and put the empire to the test of war?

options.text: Set the seal at Runnymede

modifiers.name: The Great Charter
modifiers.text: Runnymede has yielded a charter of liberties. The barons swear loyalty in exchange for written limits on royal arbitrariness.

options.text: Reject the charter: the crown is its own measure

modifiers.name: Baronial Reaction
modifiers.text: The Crown holds firm against the barons' demands. Royal authority is preserved at the price of an aggrieved aristocracy.

advances.name: Anglo-Norman Law Schools
advances.text: The Inns of Court and the law faculties of Caen and Angers, a cross-Channel jurisprudence taught in Latin and Anglo-Norman, training the magistrates of two crowns.

advances.name: The Wool Staple
advances.text: All raw English wool funnelled through a single royal staple, sealed and taxed before reaching the looms of Flanders. The crown's most lucrative monopoly.

event.title: The Wool Staple at Calais
event.text:
By royal proclamation, no fleece of English wool may pass to the looms of Flanders save through the King's staple. Sealed bales are taxed at the staple's chequer; the price of wool is set by the King's merchants; the crown's revenue from wool exceeds, in good years, all other royal income put together.

The Flemish weavers grumble. The Italian bankers extend further credit on the security of the staple. The English clothiers begin, slowly, to weave their wool at home. The Plantagenet purse has rarely been so heavy.

options.text: The wool of England, the silver of Flanders

advances.name: Garrisons of the Pale
advances.text: Marcher captains and royal garrisons hold the Lordship of Ireland, the Welsh principality and the Norman frontier as a chain of fortified districts under viceroys.

advances.name: The Great Council
advances.text: The magnum concilium of magnates and prelates, the standing Angevin advisory body that, in time, gives birth to Parliament and the Estates-General both.

advances.name: Admiralty at Arms
advances.text: The unified Plantagenet admiralty: Channel squadrons, Bay of Biscay convoys, Irish Sea patrols. A single navy for two kingdoms separated by salt water.

advances.name: Garde du Roi
advances.text: The royal household troops: gentlemen pensioners, yeomen of the guard, household cavalry. A standing core of professional soldiers loyal to the crown alone.

advances.name: Two Jurisdictions, One Crown
advances.text: English common law in the island, written civil law in the duchies, a deliberate asymmetric jurisprudence that respects custom while preserving sovereign integrity.

advances.name: Atlantic Woollens
advances.text: English broadcloth woven, fulled and dyed at home, no longer exported raw. The vertical integration of the Plantagenet textile economy.

advances.name: Redcoat Drill
advances.text: The drilled musket-and-bayonet line in scarlet, the disciplined volley fire of the Angevin regulars, redoubled by Anglo-Norman officer schools.

advances.name: Rule at Sea
advances.text: Wooden walls of the Channel, Atlantic and Mediterranean, the line-of-battle ship doctrine that makes the Angevin flag the master of three seas at once.

advances.name: Constitutional Fusion
advances.text: A bicameral assembly of lords and commons, sitting alternately in Westminster and Rouen, ratifies a written constitution binding crown, peerage and people.

advances.name: Industrial Plantagenet
advances.text: Iron of the Welsh marches, coal of the Black Country, water-powered mills along every river. The Plantagenet dominions enter the industrial age with iron and steam.

destiny.name: The Plantagenet Long Path
destiny.text: The Crown of Two Realms is bound by inheritance, but its long destiny is not yet written. Will the Plantagenet realm turn west to the salt sea and the British Isles, or south and east into the heart of France? The choice made at formation now demands a programme.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The King's Long Programme
event.text:
The chancery has drawn up a long memorandum on the Plantagenet realm's prospects. All have offered their counsel on the years to come: the clerks of Westminster, the prelates of Rouen, the seneschals of Aquitaine.

The King retires with his closest advisers to weigh what the Crown of Two Realms shall pursue beyond the immediate cares of statecraft. A long programme, written in the King's own hand and sealed with the lions, takes its place in the chancery archive at Westminster.

options.text: Set the lions on a long path

destiny.name: Pacification of the British Isles
destiny.text: The Common Law cannot reach where royal writ does not run. Bring Lothian and Gaelic Munster within the Plantagenet jurisdiction: pacify Edinburgh and the MacCarthy country at Killarney, and bind the whole archipelago to a single crown.

conditions.text: Path of Common Law of the Crown chosen
Own Edinburgh, or a subject owns it
Own Killarney, or a subject owns it
Stability at least 25

event.title: The Pacification of the Isles
event.text:
Lothian has bowed to the King's writ; the Lord Justiciar's circuit reaches now into Munster. From the cliffs of Cape Wrath to the Atlantic harbours of Cork, the same royal seal authenticates a charter, the same justices in eyre hear pleas of trespass, the same coin runs in the markets.

The British Isles are no longer a confused tangle of frontiers. They are one realm, bound by one common law beneath a single crown.

options.text: One archipelago, one crown

destiny.name: Mistress of the Narrow Seas
destiny.text: Hold the Channel from the Cinque Ports to the Flemish coast: take Antwerp and Dunkirk, the two anchors of the cloth trade, and ensure that no fleet sails between them without paying the King of England's toll. Build the war chest and raise Calais, the staple port, to half again its size.

conditions.text: Own Antwerp, or a subject owns it
Own Dunkirk, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 2000
Owns Calais and its development is at least 35

event.title: The Narrow Seas
event.text:
From the South Foreland to the dunes of Flanders, from Sandwich to Antwerp, the narrow sea is now a Plantagenet lake. The Cinque-Ports cogs convoy the wool fleets unmolested; the King's admiral collects toll from every Hansa kogge that beats up the strait.

The Channel was once the salt-water frontier that divided the Plantagenet realm. It is now its inland highway. How shall the Crown order its admiralty?

options.text: Build the King's Channel squadrons

modifiers.name: Channel Admiralty
modifiers.text: The unified squadrons of Sandwich, Portsmouth and Le Havre. The cogs and galleys of two coasts under one Lord High Admiral.

options.text: Raise the Calais staple to a royal monopoly

modifiers.name: Staple Monopoly
modifiers.text: All funnel through royal staples: the wool of England, the wine of Gascony, the cloth of Flanders. The crown's merchants set the prices of three kingdoms.

destiny.name: The Atlantic Crown
destiny.text: Plant the leopards of England in the islands of the Atlantic. Take Madeira and the Azores, build dry docks in two ports for ships that can keep the deep ocean, and raise an admiralty whose squadrons range the deep ocean from a Cinque-Ports nucleus to the Sargasso Sea.

conditions.text: Own Funchal, or a subject owns it
Own Ponta Delgada, or a subject owns it
At least 2 owned locations have a Dry Dock or a yard that replaced it
Gold at least 3000
Army size at least 75

event.title: Beyond the Western Approaches
event.text:
The leopards now flutter from the rigging of caravels lying in the harbour of Funchal; the silver-and-gold of the Azores trade rolls in to the Bristol custom-house. The dry docks of the King's ports turn out hulls that keep the open ocean for months. The Plantagenet admiralty rules a sea-empire whose extent no medieval king could have imagined.

With such reach come hard choices. Shall the King build a deep-ocean battle fleet of the western approaches, or weave a network of trading factories along the Atlantic seaboard?

options.text: A deep-ocean battle fleet

modifiers.name: Western Approaches
modifiers.text: Squadrons of the line range from Brest to the Bay of Biscay and beyond. The Plantagenet flag is the master of the deep ocean, though the army's marches grow longer.

effects.name: Maximum Ship Strength to Repair at Sea

options.text: A web of trading factories

modifiers.name: Atlantic Factories
modifiers.text: Trading factories at Funchal, Ponta Delgada and the Cape Verdes. Plantagenet merchants tap the Atlantic supply of slaves, sugar and gold.

destiny.name: Recover the Lost Duchies
destiny.text: Touraine and Maine were Henry's by right of his father, lost to the Capet at Bouvines. Recover Tours and Le Mans, and re-establish the heart of the Angevin patrimony.

conditions.text: Path of Chivalric Confederation chosen
Own Tours, or a subject owns it
Own Le Mans, or a subject owns it
Stability at least 25

event.title: The Heart of Anjou Restored
event.text:
Tours, the city of Saint Martin; Le Mans, the city of Henry's birth. The Angevin patrimony (Touraine and Maine, the heart of the Plantagenet inheritance) is restored to the family line.

The King's herald reads the homage in three languages. The bells of every parish church ring out from Angers to Rennes. The chivalry of the realm rides north from Bordeaux and south from Caen to a tournament held in the King's own hand at Le Mans.

options.text: By right of inheritance and arms

destiny.name: Empire of the Loire
destiny.text: Take Paris itself and the royal city of Orléans. Field a host of fifty thousand knights, sergeants and routiers, and make Angers, cradle of the dynasty, half again as great, a seat worthy of an emperor of the West.

conditions.text: Own Paris, or a subject owns it
Own Orléans, or a subject owns it
Army size at least 50
Owns Angers and its development is at least 42

event.title: Paris and Orléans
event.text:
The Île-de-la-Cité, Notre-Dame de Paris, the Sainte-Chapelle. Orléans on the Loire, the heart of royal France. The Capetian patrimony is in Plantagenet hands; the King of France is the Plantagenet's prisoner, his vassal, or his fugitive.

No king of the West has held both crowns since Charlemagne. Shall the Plantagenet humble the Capet line forever, or hold the Loire valley as a chivalric court where the great vassals of the realm pay homage in Eleanor's manner?

options.text: Humble the Capet: strip the Crown of France

modifiers.name: The Capet Humbled
modifiers.text: The royal fleur-de-lys lies in the dust at Westminster. The Plantagenet host moves with the momentum of a campaign that cannot be stopped.

options.text: A Loire court of palatines and homage

modifiers.name: Courts of the Loire
modifiers.text: The Loire valley becomes a court of palatine homage. The great vassals of the realm swear fealty in the manner of Poitiers, though the burghers grumble at being passed over.

destiny.name: Crown of Christendom
destiny.text: Toulouse, Dijon, Reims: the Languedoc, the Burgundian heartland, and the coronation city of the French kings. Field a Plantagenet host that no continental power can match. Crown a chivalric empire that humbles every neighbour.

conditions.text: Own Toulouse, or a subject owns it
Own Dijon, or a subject owns it
Own Reims, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 75
Army size at least 75

event.title: The Crown of Christendom
event.text:
From Toulouse in the Languedoc to Dijon in Burgundy and the coronation city of Reims, the King reigns as suzerain of the West. The leopards stand beside the eagle of the Empire as equals, perhaps as superiors. The chivalry of three crowns rides under the Plantagenet banner.

Is this an empire of arms, a martial Plantagenet imperium that humbles every continental power, or a feudal lordship of palatine vassals, knit together by oaths of homage and tournaments held in the King's hand?

options.text: An imperator of the West, by force of arms

modifiers.name: Imperator of the West
modifiers.text: Anointed at Reims, the Plantagenet stands beside the Holy Roman Emperor as an equal. The chivalry of the West rides under his banner, and the fleet is left to fend for itself.

options.text: A feudal lordship of palatine homage

modifiers.name: Palatines' Homage
modifiers.text: Counts palatine of Toulouse, Burgundy and the Languedoc bow at the King's court. Their levies and treasure flow to Westminster, at a slow but inexorable pace.

units.name: Welsh Archers
units.text: The longbowmen of Gwent and Powys, raised by Plantagenet contract. Their black-fletched yard-long arrows pierce mail and devastate cavalry charges.

units.name: Norman Knights
units.text: Mounted men-at-arms in long mail hauberks, descended from the Norman conquerors. The shock arm of the Plantagenet host.

units.name: Brabançons
units.text: Flemish and Brabantine mercenary infantry hired by the crown. Disciplined, professional and feared from Wales to Limousin.

units.name: Gascon Crossbowmen
units.text: The crossbow militias of Bordeaux, Bayonne and the Gascon ports. Disciplined urban infantry holding the southern marches.

units.name: Plantagenet Longbowmen
units.text: Massed longbow infantry trained under royal contract, the disciplined arrow storm of the Plantagenet host. The terror of French chivalry from Crécy onwards.

units.name: Household Cavalry
units.text: Gentlemen pensioners and yeomen of the guard, the King's standing household horse, mailed in the latest style and loyal to the crown alone.

units.name: Channel Cog
units.text: The clinker-built Channel cog of Sandwich and Rouen, broad of beam and tall of side. The workhorse of the Plantagenet merchant marine.

units.name: Great Ship of the Line
units.text: A first-rate ship of the line of the Angevin admiralty, broadside-armed and built to dominate the narrow seas and the Bay of Biscay.

buildings.name: Exchequer Hall
buildings.text: The chequered cloth, the pipe rolls and the writs of summons. Royal accounts are calculated by counters on a chequered table; sheriffs render their farms before the King's barons twice a year.

buildings.name: Concentric Castle
buildings.text: Concentric walls, mural towers, postern gates and a great donjon, the Plantagenet castle as perfected at Dover, Château Gaillard and Beaumaris. The most formidable fortifications in twelfth-century Europe.

buildings.name: Assize Court
buildings.text: A royal hall where the King's justices in eyre hear pleas of land, of homicide and of trespass. The crown's justice, brought to the shire by writ and seal.

buildings.name: Chivalric Tournament Field
buildings.text: The lists, the pavilions, the heralds in tabards. A licensed tournament ground where the chivalry of the realm trains in arms and competes for honour and ransom.

buildings.name: Chartered Borough
buildings.text: A self-governing town under royal charter, with its own merchant guild, court of pie-powder and farm of the borough. Burgesses pay the crown directly in lieu of seignorial dues.

buildings.name: Gascon Winery
buildings.text: The vineyards of the Garonne and Dordogne: Bordeaux, Saint-Émilion, Cahors. Claret and red wine pressed for the English Channel market and the courts of Western Christendom.

where.text: Wine is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Cinque Port Yard
buildings.text: A chartered port of the Cinque Ports confederation, sworn to provide cogs and crews to the King in exchange for self-government and a court of admiralty.

buildings.name: Anglo-Norman Law School
buildings.text: An inn of court or law faculty teaching the common law of England and the customary law of Normandy in parallel. Magistrates of the Plantagenet dual realm trained under one roof.

buildings.name: Admiralty House
buildings.text: The seat of the Lord High Admiral: drydocks, victualling yards, sail-lofts and the navy office. A unified Plantagenet admiralty with squadrons of the Channel, the Bay of Biscay and the Atlantic approaches.

buildings.name: Chivalric Palatinate
buildings.text: A great hall of palatine homage, modelled on the County Palatine of Chester and the Aquitanian ducal court at Bordeaux. Counts palatine swear fealty in the King's hand and ride out at the King's call with their full feudal hosts.

list.name: Curia Regis Itinerant
list.text: The king's household-court of justices, constables, chamberlains and clerks travelled with the Plantagenet sovereigns between Westminster, Rouen, Caen, Le Mans, Angers, Chinon and Poitiers. The Dialogus de Scaccario of Richard FitzNeal (c. 1179) describes a curia that handled fiscal audit, royal pleas, foreign correspondence and dynastic business interchangeably from wherever the king lay. It was an institution of motion: the antecedent of the sedentary Common Pleas and King's Bench that branched off only after the reforms of 1234. While well-funded the curia binds the cross-Channel realm into a single political body; when neglected, the king's household becomes a comfortable circuit and the great barons begin to resent every visitation.

list.name: Constitutions of Clarendon Apparatus
list.text: The bundle of administrative instruments codified at the Council of Clarendon in January 1164: the sixteen articles asserting royal jurisdiction over criminous clerks, the assize utrum drawing land cases into royal courts, the royal forest law administered by the King's foresters and verderers, and the chancery writ system that summoned subjects under the king's seal. The quarrel with Becket over the criminous-clerks article was bitter and ended in martyrdom at Canterbury, but the broader apparatus held: Plantagenet government became a writ-state. While maintained, royal authority reaches subjects directly through parchment rather than through the lord's intermediation; while neglected, the church remembers Becket and stability frays.

list.name: Cours Plenieres d'Aquitaine
list.text: The great curia of the duke-king at Poitiers and later Bordeaux, where the Aquitanian magnates (the counts of Angouleme, Perigord, La Marche, Armagnac and the lord of Albret) rendered counsel, heard appeals and confirmed the duchy's customary law. Eleanor of Aquitaine sustained the Poitiers court after 1168; Richard I, as count of Poitou, made it his political centre; under the later Angevins the seneschal of Gascony presided in the king's absence. Unlike the writ-state of England, ducal Aquitaine remained federal in temper: a Plantagenet province whose magnates spoke as peers rather than subjects, whose wines fed the king's host, and whose loyalty was contingent on the dignity of their consultation.

conditions.text: Any of

list.name: Cinque Ports Confederation
list.text: The Plantagenet bargain with the Channel naval towns of Hastings, New Romney, Hythe, Dover and Sandwich, joined later by the Antient Towns of Rye and Winchelsea. In return for the Ship Service of fifty-seven vessels for fifteen days each year, the ports received sweeping liberties under the Charter of 1278: their own admiralty court at Shepway, exemption from royal taxes and customs, the right to send Barons to bear the canopy at coronations, and effective immunity from the royal writ inside their walls. The Crown bought a standing fleet of the cheapest kind; the burghers got an autonomy no other English borough enjoyed. The bargain held until Henry VIII finally refitted the royal navy on different terms.

conditions.text: Any of
